samples.summary: Resolved caret `lineAffinity` is dropped by the only production consumer: `restoreLocalCursor` rebuilds the position without the field and calls `cursor.moveTo(pos)` with no affinity argument
Undo/redo selection restore strips endpoint `lineAffinity`, which the new start-defaults-to-'forward' rule turns from harmless into a rendering change
samples.evidence: `restoreSelectionFromPresence`'s local `clampPos` returns `{ blockId, offset }` only (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1974-1978), discarding the `lineAffinity` that `getPresenceSelection()` now returns on each endpoint (published by yorkie-doc-store.ts:3005 via `anchorDocRange`/`clampPosToModel`, and typed in packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:33-34). Previously dropping it was inert because every consumer defaulted to `'backward'`; this PR's documented default (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:200-206, implemented at packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260) makes an affinity-less START read `'forward'`. So an undo-restored selection whose start was recorded with an explicit `'backward'` affinity at a wrap boundary now paints beginning on the following visual line instead of where the user selected. Fix on `clampPos`: spread the endpoint's `lineAffinity` through.

samples.summary: `activeCursorPos.lineAffinity` is now typed and published, but peer caret rendering hardcodes `'backward'`, so the wire field has no effect for peers
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1561-1568 resolves every `PeerCursor.position` with a literal `'backward'`, and docs-view.tsx:226 feeds it `p.presence.activeCursorPos` — the very object whose `lineAffinity` this delta adds to `DocsPresence` (packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:27). A peer whose caret is at a wrap boundary with `'forward'` affinity is drawn one line above where their own editor draws it. The delta's own comment acknowledges the gap, so this is an unupdated consumer rather than a surprise; the fix is `peer.position.lineAffinity ?? 'backward'`.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as written. `restoreLocalCursor` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3592-3601) reconstructs the position as only `{ blockId, offset }` and calls `cursor.moveTo(...)` without an affinity argument; `Cursor.moveTo` (packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:28-32) defaults `affinity` to `'backward'` and unconditionally writes `this.lineAffinity`, which the render path reads (cursor.ts:41-49 -> resolvePositionPixel). Meanwhile the producer side genuinely preserves affinity: `anchorDocPosition(clampedPos, clampedPos.lineAffinity)` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2999) and `resolveAnchoredDocPosition` spreading `lineAffinity` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1059, 1077) feed `resolveAnchoredLocalCursor` (yorkie-doc-store.ts:1163-1182), and the new integration test cements that contract (yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:441-472). The single production consumer, docs-view.tsx:366-378, hands the resolved cursor to `restoreLocalCursor` (affinity dropped) and simultaneously to `publishResolvedLocalCursor` (affinity broadcast), so after every remote change local render and presence disagree at a wrap boundary. `validateCursorPosition` (editor.ts:960-968) early-returns and does not restore it, and `selection.setRange(range)` in the same function keeps endpoint affinity, making the caret path inconsistent with the selection path. No guard or other caller compensates; the only other references to `restoreLocalCursor` are tests. This is a changed-contract-with-unupdated-consumer across package boundaries, in the blast-radius lane.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. (1) The stripping site is exactly as described: restoreSelectionFromPresence's clampPos at packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1974-1978 rebuilds a position as `{ blockId, offset }` only, dropping lineAffinity, and is applied to both endpoints (editor.ts:1989-1990) before selection.setRange (editor.ts:1995); reachable from undoFn (editor.ts:2022) and redoFn (editor.ts:2048). (2) The input really does carry the field: getPresenceSelection returns the presence value verbatim (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2937-2952); the publisher preserves lineAffinity through clampPosToModel (yorkie-doc-store.ts:972, applied at 2994-2995 and written at 3005); the wire type declares it on anchor and focus (packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:33-34); the undo reverse is that same presence, staged by setCursorForHistory -> updateCursorPos (yorkie-doc-store.ts:2878-2884) and recorded by recordHistoryPresence (2894-2905). Local selection endpoints genuinely carry explicit affinities (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:1517-1524, 2775-2778). (3) The new default makes the loss visible: buildRects reads `start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260-261), documented at packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:200-208, and nothing re-derives affinity in between (Selection.setRange keeps endpoints as given, selection.ts:690-692; normalizeRange only reorders, selection.ts:115-128 and 708-713). So a start endpoint recorded with an explicit 'backward' at a wrap boundary repaints as 'forward' after undo/redo. No guard makes this unreachable; the only contrary text (scripts/agent/charters-ui/doc-writer.md:62-71, claiming undo/redo always clear the selection) scopes itself to a test harness with no presence and does not apply to the real YorkieDocStore path. In-lane for blast radius: a changed default on an exported rendering contract with an unupdated consumer outside the diff; major (mispainted selection, no data loss).
